subject: Rapid surge recovery & autoscale acceptance — post-call follow-up
messages:

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Rapid surge recovery & autoscale acceptance — post-call follow-up

Hi Stella / Nate —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call focused on the SLOs you emphasized: 95th p99 latency targets for streaming responses (target 300ms p95 for single-turn, p99 sub-second for streaming commit tokens), and the burst scenarios (traffic spikes up to 12k concurrent requests for ~90s).

Concrete items we captured:
- Desired SLOs: p95 <= 300ms for regular generation; p99 streaming commit latency < 1s.
- Burst profile: baseline 1.2k concurrency; peak bursts to 12k for ~60–120s, expected ~3–4 times per day during business hours.
- Warm pool preference: you want 20% of peak prewarmed (approx 2.4k instances) versus cold start queueing.
- Queueing tolerance: BrightMart accepts up to 6s head-of-line queueing for best-effort tiers, but <1s for premium traffic.

Next steps we discussed:
1) Redwood to propose a short acceptance test plan that verifies scale-up times, warm-pool priming behavior, and queueing under mixed-priority traffic.
2) Delivery of the test plan and expected artifacts by EOD tomorrow (I assigned Karthik to own the test definition).
3) BrightMart to provide a recent traffic trace and confirmation of premium vs best-effort percentages by Tuesday.

Attaching the initial burst SLO test plan draft and an example warm-pool priming log for reference.

Cheers,
Sean

--
Sean Gallagher

Sean — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 12k spike number is concurrent token-generation sessions, not purely websocket connections — some sessions stream for longer than others. Peak durations are usually 45–90s.
- Premium traffic is ~18% of overall requests but drives 60% of revenue — for acceptance we need guaranteed premium SLOs.
- We can share a 24hr traffic trace (anonymized) by tomorrow AM.

We reviewed the attached plan quickly. Key asks: include a validation step for the KV cache population time (we've seen stalls when KV caches were cold) and an explicit canary rollback threshold if p99 latency goes above 1.5s for premium.

Stella

--

Sean / team —

Thanks, I sketched out test steps and timelines inline with Stella's asks. Highlights:

- Test plan summary (see attachment stub):
  * Phase A: Baseline verification — validate steady-state p95/p99 for single-turn and streaming with typical concurrency (1.2k).
  * Phase B: Controlled burst — replay trace scaled to 12k concurrency; measure scale-up time and queue depth. Validate warm pool contribution vs cold starts.
  * Phase C: KV priming run — verify KV cache hit ramp and worst-case cache-miss latencies.
  * Phase D: Canary rollback thresholds — automatic rollback if premium p99 > 1.5s for >2 consecutive minutes.

- Success criteria: premium traffic p99 < 1.0s during burst (goal), p95 < 300ms steady state, scale-up to 80% of peak capacity within 20s of burst onset using warm pool + autoscale.

- Data we need from BrightMart: a 24hr trace, allocation of premium vs best-effort flags, and a sample streaming session shape.

I'll upload a proper PDF variant to the BRG-231 test folder and tag Marissa for test orchestration.

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sean / Karthik —

We uploaded the 24hr trace to the link you shared and included the premium flag column. One quick ask: during the controlled burst can you ensure you run two variants — one with warm pool at 20% of peak and one at 5% — we want to quantify cost vs acceptance tradeoff.

Also, our ops team asked about warm-pool priming duration: what's the typical idle-to-ready time for prewarmed containers/instances in your platform? If it's variable, please indicate the distribution.

Nate

Subject: Re: Rapid surge recovery & autoscale acceptance — post-call follow-up

Appreciate the quick upload, Nate. A few clarifying notes and our commitments: 

- We'll run the two controlled-burst variants (20% warm pool and 5% warm pool) and report delta on cost and p99 exposure.
- Typical prewarmed instance readiness: median ~8s, 90th percentile ~18s, 99th ~35s (distribution observed across GPU families and model sizes). We'll include a small table of the measured distribution in the final report.
- For KV priming, we'll add explicit instrumentation to measure first-read miss latency and time-to-80% cache hit during ramp.
- Canary rollback policy: implement the threshold Karthik suggested; we'll simulate a failure mode and demonstrate automatic rollback in the canary run.

Action owners & deadlines:
- Karthik: finalize test plan PDF and upload to Drive (ETA: 2027-04-20 17:00 PDT).
- Marissa: schedule the controlled-burst runs in our test cluster and collect telemetry (ETA: 2027-04-22).
- BrightMart: confirm premium traffic tagging and notify when replay is ready for Redwood (ETA: 2027-04-20 09:00 PDT — done).

I'll follow up with results and a short recording of the canary rollback demo.

Best,
Sean
